metadata.title: An even-strand Markov calculus for classical and virtual links

description.en: The Creative Commons Attribution license allows re-distribution and re-use of a licensed work on the condition that the creator is appropriately credited.

metadata.description:
We give an explicit elementary affirmative answer to the ordinary-closure interpretation of Problem 42 in the 2014 survey of Fenn, Ilyutko, Kauffman and Manturov. Four reversible algebraic schemes classify ordinary oriented unframed classical link closures using only even-strand braid states. Four additional exchange schemes give the corresponding statement for oriented virtual links. The proof converts the established unrestricted Markov theorems by positively stabilizing every odd-strand vertex and explicitly lifting every generating edge.

Arbitrary finite word blocks and syntactic support bounds are part of the formulation. Minimality, uniform geometric locality, a certificate-search algorithm, historical priority and present openness are not claimed. The note compares its additional schemes with Fiedler's negative conjugation-plus-double-move result without independently certifying his full counterexample proof. It explicitly credits Nencka's related 1996 power-of-two braid announcement; its generalized equivalence and ordinary-closure interpretation are not certified from the two-page source, and historical priority is not asserted. The accompanying compact verification package contains the standalone source, standard-library Python diagnostics, exact results, source qualifications and licenses; finite checks supplement the universal proof. Source-bound literal nonempty left-exchange controls separately verify the index shift and retained buffer. Fuller related Nencka1998/1999 texts have been identified but not accessed, so their bearing on exact ordinary-closure priority remains unresolved.

AI tools were used extensively in construction, drafting, adversarial review and computational verification. This research note is unrefereed; no human peer review or formal proof certification is claimed. The new manuscript and documentation are licensed under CC BY 4.0, and the Python code under MIT.

Incomplete priority review: We could not obtain the full texts of Nencka's identified 1998 article, 1999 chapter, or catalogued 1996 preprint CPT96/P.3381. The priority review is therefore incomplete, and historical ordinary-closure priority remains unresolved. This note establishes the displayed formulation from explicitly credited unrestricted theorems; it does not establish a historically new resolution. Unavailable text is not evidence of absence or invalidity of earlier work.
